title: Neon PostgreSQL foundation (authoritative transactional store)
objective: Implement the authoritative Neon PostgreSQL foundation defined by verified INFRA-001 without changing the existing v1 request path.
acceptance_criteria: DocumentStore port applies P016 persistence discipline for document registry, append-only version chain, idempotency records and command log.
Neon adapter uses pooled connections, idempotent DDL, byte-preserving JSON semantics where required, and advisory-lock/CAS serialization.
MemoryDocumentStore exists for local development and deterministic tests.
FailClosedDocumentStore provides typed fail-closed behavior when production persistence is unconfigured.
Cross-backend fixtures prove byte-identical canonical persisted views.
CAS conflict and idempotency retry behavior are deterministic and tested.
CI exercises the adapter against a real PostgreSQL service.
Existing v1 request behavior is unchanged.
No R2, WireEnvelope v2, stateless request migration, Redis, worker service, or production environment wiring is introduced.
non_goals: No request-shape change or WireEnvelope v2.
risk_assumptions: P016Persist is the architectural persistence precedent.
Neon is authoritative for transactional state; Redis and workers are not part of this work item.
Production remains fail-closed until INFRA-007 wiring.
Document persistence must not become a competing Construction Graph authority.
evidence_requirements: Exact CI run using a real PostgreSQL service.
Governance/schema validation and changed-file scope proof.

transitions.reason: INFRA-001 is VERIFIED and its roadmap explicitly releases INFRA-002 as the dependency-ordered Neon successor. The implementation scope and evidence contract are frozen in the issue and successor prompt.
